findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body: When a caller invokes the returned disposer, the registered `"message"` handler remains active. Subsequent messages can therefore reach torn-down components, while repeated attach/dispose cycles retain captured state and cause duplicate processing and unbounded listener growth. The PR description says existing contracts should be preserved, but this removes the cleanup behavior entirely.

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup function
findings.body:
Calling the disposer returned by `attach` no longer unregisters the `"message"` handler. Any later message still invokes callbacks after cancellation/teardown, and repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate active listeners, causing stale or duplicate processing.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup function
findings.body:
After callers invoke the returned cleanup function, subsequent `"message"` events still execute the handler. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles also accumulate listeners, causing duplicate processing and memory leaks.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore message-handler removal during teardown
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup function no longer detaches the listener. Any socket message received afterward still reaches a handler whose session/component was torn down, allowing untrusted peers to trigger stale privileged logic; repeated attach/cleanup cycles also accumulate callbacks and amplify resource consumption.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup function no longer unregisters the handler. With a long-lived socket, repeated attach/cleanup cycles retain every handler and its captured objects, cause duplicate message processing, grow memory and per-message work without bound, and may trigger `MaxListenersExceededWarning`.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
